title: Display and Visibility Claims
summary: Check retailer display, shelf and branding claims against the agreed programme, outlet list and photo proof, and catch reused, mismatched or missing photos before finance pays.

seo.title: Display and Visibility Claims Verification | VipraTech
seo.description: Verify retailer display, visibility and shop-branding claims against programme terms, outlet lists and photo proof, and flag reused or missing photos.

problem.intro: Brands pay retailers, often through distributors, to display products in prime spots, run branded shelves and put up signage. Each month, claims arrive for a list of outlets, backed by photos from the field team or the retailer. Few teams can check thousands of photos against the programme.

pain_points.title: Photos reused across months and outlets
pain_points.detail: The same photo, or a near copy, is submitted for different outlets or periods.

pain_points.title: Outlets outside the programme
pain_points.detail: Payments are claimed for outlets that were never enrolled, were dropped or exceed the programme's slots.

pain_points.title: Rates and periods applied loosely
pain_points.detail: Display rates differ by outlet class, display type and period, and claims mix them up.

pain_points.title: No time to look
pain_points.detail: With thousands of photos a month, teams check a sample and pay the rest.

solution.overview: VipraTech reads display claims with their outlet lists and photos, and checks each line against the programme: is the outlet enrolled for this display type and period, is the rate right for its class, and is there a photo. Every photo is checked for date and location data where available, and compared with earlier submissions to catch reused or near-duplicate images. Lines that pass go to the credit note sheet; the rest go to trade marketing or finance with the reason and the photo side by side. Judging whether a display met the agreed standard can be added later with shelf recognition.
capabilities: Programme register with enrolled outlets, display types, rates and periods
Checks every claimed outlet and period against the programme
Detects reused and near-duplicate photos across outlets and months
Reads photo date and location data where the image has it
Review screen with the claim line and photo side by side
Credit note sheet and programme spend report by region and outlet class

workflow.title: Receive claims and photos
workflow.detail: Claims arrive with outlet lists and photos, by upload, email or from the field app.

workflow.title: Match to the programme
workflow.detail: Each outlet is matched to the enrolled list, display type, rate and period.

workflow.title: Check the photos
workflow.detail: Photos are checked for presence, date and location data, and reuse across outlets and months.

workflow.title: Recalculate
workflow.detail: The eligible amount is recalculated from the programme rate for each outlet.

workflow.title: Review
workflow.detail: Trade marketing or finance reviews flagged lines with the photo and the reason.

workflow.title: Approve and pay
workflow.detail: Finance approves the credit note sheet, and spend is reported by region and outlet class.

match_rules.logic: The outlet must be on the programme list for the claim month, with the display type it was enrolled for.
Photos must be taken within the claim period. Timestamps and metadata are used where they exist, and photos without them count as weaker evidence.
Each photo is compared with every earlier display photo by image fingerprint, so a photo reused across outlets or months is caught even when cropped or resized.
The photo is checked for the agreed brand and display type. Doubtful photos go to a person rather than straight to rejection.
Payment is the programme rate times the months that qualified, held to the programme budget.

exception_codes.meaning: The outlet is not on the programme for that month.
exception_codes.action: Reject, or add the outlet if it was enrolled late.

exception_codes.meaning: The photo matches one already used for another outlet or month.
exception_codes.action: Reject the month and flag the outlet.

exception_codes.meaning: The photo was taken outside the claim period.
exception_codes.action: Ask for a photo from the period.

exception_codes.meaning: The brand or display type cannot be confirmed from the photo.
exception_codes.action: A reviewer looks at the photo and decides.

exception_codes.meaning: Approved payments would exceed the programme budget.

inputs: Photos from the field app, distributors or retailers
Display programme with enrolled outlets, rates and periods
outputs: Claim lines checked against the programme
Credit note sheet for finance approval

human_in_the_loop: Trade marketing decides on any photo or outlet the system flags, and finance approves every credit note sheet. The system flags doubtful photos; it does not reject them on its own.
integrations: Field sales app or SFA photo exports
ERP such as SAP or Tally for credit notes
guardrails: No payment for outlets outside the enrolled programme
Possibly reused photos held until a person reviews them
Every decision keeps the photo and the reason
compliance_notes: Display payments are often settled through distributors by credit note; the system keeps the link from programme to claim to credit note for audit.

rollout.scope: One display programme in one region, with one month of settled display claims as the benchmark.
deliverables: Photo checks on one month of claims

what_we_measure.how: Reused or missing photos flagged, confirmed by trade marketing.
Claims for outlets outside the programme, confirmed by finance.
Time spent reviewing a month of display claims, compared with today.

faqs.q: Can it tell whether the display was actually set up well?
faqs.a: Not in the first version. It checks the outlet, period, rate and whether the photo is genuine and new. Judging the display itself can be added with shelf recognition once there are enough labelled photos.

faqs.q: Our photos come through WhatsApp. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: No. Photos can be collected from WhatsApp exports, uploads or the field app. Photos sent through WhatsApp often lose their date and location data, so the reuse check matters more.

faqs.q: How does it detect reused photos?
faqs.a: Each photo is compared with earlier submissions using image fingerprints that survive cropping and resizing, and close matches are shown side by side.

faqs.q: Is this the same system as your distributor claims settlement?
faqs.a: Yes. Every VipraTech workflow runs on one claims engine: the document reading, matching, review queue and audit trail are shared. For this workflow we set up your display programme as versioned rules, along with your document templates and matching keys.
